resume.heading: Resume
resume.intro: A brief overview of my education, skills, and goals.
resume.shooterTitle: Multiplayer Shooter - Developer (Built-in RP, Mirror, UI Toolkit)
resume.shooterDescription: Designed the network architecture and client-server player synchronization using the Mirror framework (Built-in Render Pipeline). Implemented lag compensation, state interpolation, and shooting logic. Created a custom weapon customization interface with UI Toolkit.
resume.racingTitle: Racing Game Project - Developer (Built-in RP, Raycast Physics)
resume.racingDescription: Developed an arcade racing game with a strong focus on vehicle physics. Implemented engine torque curve simulation, tire friction/grip models, and tuned vehicle handling for drifting and high-speed stability.
resume.rtsTitle: RTS Game - Developer (Universal Render Pipeline / URP)
resume.rtsDescription: Developing a real-time strategy game using URP. Implemented unit selection and command systems, pathfinding AI, and resource management. Optimized graphics and shaders for URP scene lighting.
resume.gamefestDescription: Placed 19th out of 100 participants in the “Two Realities” Game Jam. Built a 2D platformer from scratch in 36 hours, implementing dimension-switching mechanics and character controls.
resume.skillsSummary: I have been working with Unity for over five years, focusing on application and gameplay logic as well as C# application architecture. I can build multiplayer games with the Mirror framework and develop projects using both Built-in RP and URP. I understand OOP principles and design patterns, and build C# / .NET applications and tools. I can comfortably read technical documentation in English (B2).

about.title: About - My Portfolio
about.heading: About me
about.intro: Who I am, what interests me, and where I want to go.
about.paragraphOne: I am studying software engineering at university and have been passionate about developing games in Unity for over five years. I started my GameDev journey with small projects (shooters, racing games, and puzzles) and gradually moved on to building complex custom mechanics from scratch-from a custom vehicle physics controller to object interaction systems.
about.paragraphTwo: I have hands-on experience designing multiplayer games with the Mirror framework, as well as working with URP and the Built-in Render Pipeline. I continue to deepen my knowledge of C# and architectural patterns, and explore frameworks and techniques for optimizing game logic. In May 2026, I took part in the GameFest hackathon in Tashkent for the first time. I built a 2D platformer solo in 36 hours for the “Two Realities” Game Jam and placed 19th out of 100 participants.
